summary: This lecture from Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) Part 87 covers Islamic etiquette regarding seeking permission to enter homes and respecting privacy. Sheikh Ali Mashhour discusses the Prophet's teachings on knocking three times, standing to the side of doors to avoid looking inside, and the importance of not invading others' privacy through spying or surveillance. The lecture emphasizes that seeking permission involves asking both to enter physically and to look inside, establishing the principle that Muslims have a right to privacy. The teaching extends to broader concepts of concealing others' faults, avoiding character assassination, and recognizing that all people have weaknesses. The lecture concludes with guidance on sneezing and yawning etiquette, explaining that sneezing indicates alertness (which Allah loves) while yawning indicates laziness (which is from Satan).
